subject.title: fix(codex): guard subagent monitor against missing task runId

question: Should a Codex-native task without its synthetic run ID be treated as a supported recoverable persisted state, or as an invariant violation that must be repaired or terminalized by the task owner?
rationale: The PR provides no real example of the state, and the choice determines whether silently retaining an untrackable running row is intentional compatibility behavior or a hidden state leak.

options.title: Repair at task ownership
options.body: Require the mirror or registry restore path to reconstruct or terminalize malformed Codex-native rows and remove the monitor skip.

options.title: Support monitor tolerance
options.body: Keep the skip only with live evidence, an explicit cleanup policy, diagnostics, and tests proving malformed rows cannot remain active indefinitely.

recommendation.title: Repair at task ownership
recommendation.body: Require the mirror or registry restore path to reconstruct or terminalize malformed Codex-native rows and remove the monitor skip.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history ties the native task mirror and synthetic run identity to this owner boundary.
